newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals mostly firmer, bullion weak.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals mostly firmer, bullion weak.

text.p: Yen-based precious metal futures ended mostly firmer in Tokyo on Monday, as a weakening of the yen against the dollar offset a slight fall in bullion prices.

Traders said the bullion market turned quiet after an early dip that extended New York's losses on Friday. The market was expected to continue consolidating into the year-end holidays after slumping to three-year lows early this month.
TOCOM benchmark October 1997 gold ended flat at 1,334 yen per gram, while the other months were one to three yen better.
Bullion closed at $368.20/50 an ounce, down marginally from Friday's New York closing quote of $368.45/95.
Gold bullion has held mostly within a $367.50 to $370.00 range for the past week, attempting to consolidate after slumping to a three-year low of $365.70 two weeks ago.
One trader said funds appeared to be comfortable with their short positions and in no hurry to cover, although he expected bullion prices to find support at $367.

Platinum bullion also remained weak and at a discount to gold despite uncertainty surrounding Japan-Russia talks on next year's supply contracts, which were postponed from their usual mid-December date due to a delay in Russia's budget. One trader said the uncertainty was already factored into the markets.

Yen-based platinum prices nevertheless ended mostly firmer due to the weaker yen, while first-position December futures were supported by talk that investors still holding long positions in the contract would take delivery of physical metal when it expires, traders said.
TOCOM benchmark October platinum settled three yen higher at 1,342 yen per gram, while bullion prices were at $367.75/50, down from Friday's Tokyo close of $369.00/75.
TOCOM October palladium ended one better at 430 yen per gram. October silver was up 0.5 at 178.0 yen per 10 grams.
